title: Jesus, Thy Church with Longing Eyes
description: Jesus, Thy Church with Longing Eyes in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Hiley Bathurst wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 144.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, Thy Church with long-ing eyes For Thine ex-pect-ed com-ing waits: When will the pro-mised light a-rise, And glo-ry beam from Zi-on’s gates?

lines: Jesus, Thy Church with longing eyes
For Thine expected coming waits:
When will the promised light arise,
And glory beam from Zion’s gates?
E’en now, when tempests round us fall
And wintry clouds o’ercast the sky,
Thy words with pleasure we recall
And deem that our redemption’s nigh.
Come, gracious Lord, our hearts renew,
Our foes repel, our wrongs redress,
Man’s rooted enmity subdue,
And crown Thy Gospel with success.
O come and reign o’er every land;
Let Satan from his throne be hurled,
All nations bow to Thy command,
And grace revive a dying world.
Teach us in watchfulness and prayer
To wait for the appointed hour
And fit us by Thy grace to share
The triumphs of Thy conquering power.

licence: Public domain: William Hiley Bathurst died in 1877.
credits: Words by William Hiley Bathurst (1796–1877), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
